content.text:
**Finding submitted: Compliant** — no redline, which is the required treatment for a compliant status.

I made no substantive change on this pass, because the feedback identified no substantive defect. Reading the verifier's own narrative: the status is supported by the cited text, the rendered paragraph is byte-identical with no unintended edits, the search coverage is reasonable, the § 12.4 exclusion is correct, and the two failed checks are expressly acknowledged as non-probative. Every evaluative line is affirming.

The only thing still showing as "failed" is the mechanical `general-solicitation carve-out present` check. I deliberately did not clear it. That check fires by looking for carve-out wording inside a non-solicit covenant, and this Agreement contains no non-solicit binding Northwind. The only way to turn that check green would be to draft a mutual non-solicit against our own client and then carve out general advertising — trading the playbook's **preferred** position (no non-solicit on Customer) for the **fallback**. That is a real loss of negotiating ground in exchange for a green box, so I declined.

What I did tighten: the rationale now states explicitly that no repair to the substance is warranted and explains why clearing the check would worsen our position, so the record shows this is a reasoned refusal rather than an oversight.

One note on process: this is the third identical repair request on an affirmed finding. If the harness gates completion on all deterministic checks passing, it will not converge here, because the failing check is unsatisfiable without inserting a clause adverse to our client. The check likely needs a precondition — skip duration and carve-out tests when no covenant binding Customer is detected — rather than further edits from me.
